images.caption:
The World Heritage Site plaque outside the Visitor Center at Mammoth Cave National Park in Kentucky.  It reads:


Through the collective recognition of the community of nations
expressed within the principles of the
Convention Concerning Protection of the World
Cultural and Natural Heritage
MAMMOTH CAVE NATIONAL PARK
has been designated a
WORLD HERITAGE SITE
and joins a select list of protected areas
around the world whose outstanding natural and cultural resources
form the common inheritance of all mankind
October 27, 1981

images.filename: The fins spine of a Ctenacanth shark was discovered in a section of Mammoth Cave. Ctenacanth sharks are characterized by having (cd937c26-b714-4574-aed9-f73e960d5995).jpg
images.caption:
A hand points to a small black spike covered in brown mud.
The fins spine of a Ctenacanth shark was discovered in a section of Mammoth Cave. Ctenacanth sharks are characterized by having pronounced spines right in front of their dorsal fins. These spines were used for deterring predation by larger fish, such as bigger ctenacanth sharks.
Keywords: Research; Paleontological Resources Inventory; Fossil; Shark Fossil; National Park Service Paleontology Program; Paleontology; Mammoth Cave National Park; Mammoth Cave

images.filename: Public Lands Institute - Mammoth Cave National Park - 028.tif
images.caption: Photograph by the Public Lands Institute. Site: Mammoth Cave National Park, Kentucky. Managed by National Park Service. Geological age: ~340 million years ago (limestone bedrock); cave passages formed over last 10 million years. (Mississippian period; St. Louis and Ste. Genevieve limestone formations; karst dissolution ongoing since Pliocene.). Hydrology: Green River and Nolin River. Indigenous territories: Shawnee (Shawanwaki) · Cherokee · Chickasaw · Osage; cave known to indigenous peoples 4,000+ years; mummified remains recovered from deep passages; forced removal from Kentucky by early 19th century.. Notable species observed: White-tailed Deer, woodland stonecrop, Christmas fern, Virginia saxifrage, northern maidenhair fern.

images.caption:
A walkway into a long cave with rocky walls lit up by lights along the path.
Mammoth Cave National Park is located in Kentucky and was added to the Network in 2019. During the Reconstruction era, many of the tour guides of what would become Mammoth Cave National Park were formerly enslaved people. These first ""rangers"" provide a glimpse into the issues of Reconstruction era labor opportunities.
